@@ -0,0 +1,28 @@
+## #29 - Sign the Inno-embedded uninstaller (2026-11-08)
+
+- **Chosen:** ISCC signs both the setup exe and the embedded uninstaller
+  through Inno Setup's named sign tool. `installer.ps1` asks
+  `sign.ps1 -Status` whether a certificate is configured; if so it passes
+  `/DSignToolName=camcraft` (the `.iss` turns on `SignTool=` and
+  `SignedUninstaller=yes` only under that define) and
+  `/Scamcraft=powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File
+  $q<sign.ps1>$q -Path $f`. `sign.ps1` stays the only reader of
+  `CAMCRAFT_SIGN_*` and the only place holding the signtool command and
+  the timestamp URL; secrets reach the ISCC child through the inherited
+  environment, never its command line.
+- **Without a certificate:** no `/D`, no `/S`; the compile is the same
+  command as before plus a named log line ("installer signing: off").
+- **Dropped:** the separate `sign.ps1 -Path <setup.exe>` pass after
+  ISCC in `release.ps1` and `release.yml`. ISCC now signs the setup exe
+  itself; a second pass would re-sign (a second timestamp request) for
+  nothing. `installer.ps1` checks the setup exe carries a signature when
+  signing is on, so an ISCC that skipped the tool fails the build.
+- **Also fixed in passing:** `release.yml`'s installer step had no
+  `CAMCRAFT_SIGN_CERT_PASSWORD` in its env (only the earlier sign step
+  had it), so with the secret set its `sign.ps1` call would have failed
+  as half-configured. The step now carries it.
+- **Considered and dropped:** a sign tool defined in the `.iss`
+  (`SignTool=signtool ...`): it would duplicate the signtool command and
+  the certificate selection in a second file. A `$p`-parameterised tool
+  passing thumbprint/PFX args from installer.ps1: same duplication, and
+  it would put the PFX password on ISCC's command line.

@@ -1,6 +1,8 @@
 # Installer build (M13.3): compiles scripts/installer/camcraft.iss with
 # Inno Setup against an already-staged dist tree (the zip's) and writes
-# dist/camcraft-<ver>-win-x64-setup.exe beside the zip.
+# dist/camcraft-<ver>-win-x64-setup.exe beside the zip. With a certificate
+# configured (CAMCRAFT_SIGN_*, scripts/sign.ps1) ISCC signs the setup exe
+# and its embedded uninstaller; without one both stay unsigned, as before.
 #
 # Usage: powershell -File scripts/installer.ps1 -Version 0.8.0 `
 #            [-Stage dist/camcraft-0.8.0-win-x64] [-OutDir dist] [-Required]
@@ -53,12 +55,42 @@ $stageAbs = (Resolve-Path $Stage).Path
 $outAbs = (Resolve-Path $OutDir).Path
 $iss = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "installer\camcraft.iss"
 
-# ---- 3. Compile ---------------------------------------------------------
-$isccArgs = @("/Qp", "/DAppVersion=$Version", "/DStageDir=$stageAbs", "/DOutDir=$outAbs", $iss)
+# ---- 3. Signing: sign.ps1 decides, ISCC calls it ------------------------
+# sign.ps1 -Status is the one reader of CAMCRAFT_SIGN_*. Configured, ISCC
+# gets a sign tool named "camcraft" that runs sign.ps1 on each file it
+# signs ($f = the quoted file, $q = a quote; Inno Setup SignTool syntax),
+# and the .iss turns on SignTool + SignedUninstaller, so the setup exe AND
+# the uninstaller embedded in it are signed by the same signtool command
+# and timestamp server as the release exes. Not configured, no sign tool
+# is passed and the build is byte-for-byte today's unsigned one.
+$signScript = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "sign.ps1"
+& powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $signScript -Status
+$signStatus = $LASTEXITCODE
+$signArgs = @()
+if ($signStatus -eq 0) {
+    # Single-quoted: $q and $f are ISCC's placeholders, not PowerShell's.
+    $tool = 'powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $q' + $signScript + '$q -Path $f'
+    $signArgs = @("/DSignToolName=camcraft", "/Scamcraft=$tool")
+    Write-Host "installer signing: on (setup exe and embedded uninstaller, via sign.ps1)"
+} elseif ($signStatus -eq 10) {
+    Write-Host "installer signing: off (no certificate configured); setup and uninstaller ship unsigned"
+} else {
+    Fail "sign.ps1 -Status exited with $signStatus (signing half-configured)"
+}
+
+# ---- 4. Compile ---------------------------------------------------------
+$isccArgs = @("/Qp", "/DAppVersion=$Version", "/DStageDir=$stageAbs", "/DOutDir=$outAbs") + $signArgs + @($iss)
 Write-Host "> ISCC $($isccArgs -join ' ')"
 & $iscc @isccArgs
 if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Fail "ISCC exited with $LASTEXITCODE" }
 $setup = Join-Path $outAbs "camcraft-$Version-win-x64-setup.exe"
 if (-not (Test-Path $setup)) { Fail "ISCC succeeded but $setup is missing" }
+if ($signArgs.Count -gt 0) {
+    # sign.ps1 already ran signtool verify on each file ISCC handed it; this
+    # catches an ISCC that silently skipped the sign tool.
+    $sig = Get-AuthenticodeSignature $setup
+    if (-not $sig.SignerCertificate) { Fail "signing is configured but $setup carries no signature" }
+    Write-Host "setup signed by: $($sig.SignerCertificate.Subject)"
+}
 Write-Host "Installer: $setup"
 exit 0

@@ -11,11 +11,21 @@
 #   CAMCRAFT_SIGN_TIMESTAMP_URL   optional RFC-3161 server override
 #
 # Usage: powershell -File scripts/sign.ps1 -Path a.exe, b.exe
+#        powershell -File scripts/sign.ps1 -Status   (configured? see below)
+#
+# -Status answers "is a certificate configured?" without signing anything:
+# exit 0 configured, exit 10 not configured (prints the unsigned line), exit
+# 1 half-configured. installer.ps1 asks it before wiring Inno Setup's
+# SignTool, so this file stays the one place that reads CAMCRAFT_SIGN_*.
+# Inno Setup calls this script as its sign tool for the setup exe AND the
+# uninstaller it embeds (installer.ps1, /Scamcraft=...), so the signtool
+# command and the timestamp server below are the only ones in the repo.
 # Exit 0 when unsigned-by-configuration or signed and verified; exit 1 when a
 # certificate IS configured but signing cannot proceed (missing signtool,
 # missing file, signtool failure) - a configured-but-broken setup is an error.
 param(
-    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string[]]$Path,
+    [string[]]$Path = @(),
+    [switch]$Status,
     [string]$Description = "camcraft",
     [string]$TimestampUrl = ""
 )

+    if ($Status) { exit 10 }
     exit 0
 }
+if ($Status) { exit 0 }
+if ($Path.Count -eq 0) { Fail "-Path is required (the files to sign)" }
